# sampling.library: BlueNoisePoints2D

```plato

    // About `count` blue-noise points over the region: a saturated Poisson-disk
    // set at the radius the count implies, thinned to exactly the count when the
    // region held enough. Thirty darts per cell is the figure
    // `PoissonDiskPattern2D` names.
    BlueNoisePoints2D(region: Bounds2D, count: Integer, seed: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => ThinnedPoints2D(count,
            PoissonDiskPoints2D(region, BlueNoiseRadius(region, count), 30, seed));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: BlueNoisePattern2D): Array<Point2D>
        => BlueNoisePoints2D(self.Region, self.Count, self.Seed);

    //==
    // # Repulsion relaxation
    //
    // Any point set becomes more even if every point is pushed away from its
    // close neighbours and the push is repeated. That is the cheap half of what
    // Lloyd's algorithm does, and it is what turns white noise into something
    // blue without any radius bookkeeping.
    //
    // LLOYD'S ALGORITHM ITSELF IS NOT HERE, and the reason is worth writing down.
    // Lloyd moves each point to the centroid of its Voronoi cell; discretized, it
    // dices the region into stones, assigns each stone to its nearest point, and
    // averages. The assignment has to be STORED — computed once per stone and then
    // read once per point — or the pass degrades from stones times points to
    // stones times points squared. This vocabulary's arrays are immutable lazy
    // values with no in-place write, so storing it needs an affine builder, and
    // the builders have no runtime on several of the backends these bodies are
    // meant to reach. Repulsion needs no such table: each point reads the others
    // directly. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd%27s_algorithm

    // Where point `index` goes after one repulsion pass: the sum of the pushes
    // away from every neighbour inside `radius`, each falling linearly to zero at
    // that radius, scaled by `strength` and clamped back into the region.
    // Coincident points do not push each other, having no direction to push along.
    RepelledPoint2D(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>, radius: Number,
        strength: Number, index: Integer): Point2D
    {
        var p = points[index];
        var push = Vector2D(0.0, 0.0);
        var j = 0;
        while (j < points.Count)
        {
            var d = p.Distance(points[j]);
            if (j != index && d > 0.0 && d < radius)
            {
                push = push + points[j].Between(p) * ((radius - d) / d);
            }
            j = j + 1;
        }
        return Point2D((p.X + strength * push.X).Clamp(region.Min.X, region.Max.X),
                       (p.Y + strength * push.Y).Clamp(region.Min.Y, region.Max.Y));
    }

    // The point set after one repulsion pass. Every point moves from the same
    // starting configuration — the pass is a simultaneous step, not a sweep — so
    // the result does not depend on the order the points are stored in.
    RepelledPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>, radius: Number,
        strength: Number): Array<Point2D>
    {
        var moved = Point2D.NoPoints;
        var i = 0;
        while (i < points.Count)
        {
            moved = moved.Append(RepelledPoint2D(region, points, radius, strength, i));
            i = i + 1;
        }
        return moved;
    }

    // The point set after `passes` repulsion passes. A `strength` of about 0.2
    // and a `radius` of about the mean spacing converge in a handful of passes;
    // a larger strength oscillates. Each pass measures every point against every
    // other, so this is for hundreds of points, not for millions.
    RelaxedPoints2D(region: Bounds2D, points: Array<Point2D>, radius: Number,
        strength: Number, passes: Integer): Array<Point2D>
        => passes <= 0
            ? points
            : RelaxedPoints2D(region, RepelledPoints2D(region, points, radius, strength),
                radius, strength, passes - 1);

    //==
    // # Pattern generators in space
    //
    // The closed-form families one dimension up. Poisson-disk and blue noise stop
    // at two dimensions: their background grid is written to as it fills, and in
    // three dimensions the sliding window the planar sweep gets away with becomes
    // a whole plane of occupancy that would have to be carried and indexed. The
    // plastic (R3) sequence is the even spatial scatter to reach for meanwhile.

    // Count Halton points through the volume, taken from index one.
    HaltonPoints3D(region: Bounds3D, count: Integer, baseX: Integer, baseY: Integer,
        baseZ: Integer): Array<Point3D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitCube(HaltonPoint3D(i + 1, baseX, baseY, baseZ)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: HaltonPattern3D): Array<Point3D>
        => HaltonPoints3D(self.Region, self.Count, self.BaseX, self.BaseY, self.BaseZ);

    // Count plastic (R3) points through the volume.
    PlasticPoints3D(region: Bounds3D, count: Integer, offset: Number): Array<Point3D>
        => count.MapRange(i => region.FromUnitCube(PlasticPoint3D(i, offset)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: PlasticPattern3D): Array<Point3D>
        => PlasticPoints3D(self.Region, self.Count, self.Offset);

    // The point of grid cell (i, j, k), jittered from the cell center.
    JitteredCellPoint3D(region: Bounds3D, cellCounts: IntegerVector3, jitter: Number,
        seed: Integer, i: Integer, j: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var o = FeatureOffset3D(seed, i, j, k, jitter);
        return Point3D(
            region.Min.X + (i.ToNumber + o.X) * (region.Max.X - region.Min.X) / cellCounts.X.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Y + (j.ToNumber + o.Y) * (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y) / cellCounts.Y.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Z + (k.ToNumber + o.Z) * (region.Max.Z - region.Min.Z) / cellCounts.Z.ToNumber);
    }

    // One point per grid cell, X fastest then Y then Z.
    // Precondition: every cell count is positive.
    JitteredGridPoints3D(region: Bounds3D, cellCounts: IntegerVector3, jitter: Number,
        seed: Integer): Array<Point3D>
        => (cellCounts.X * cellCounts.Y * cellCounts.Z).MapRange(n =>
            JitteredCellPoint3D(region, cellCounts, jitter, seed,
                n % cellCounts.X, n / cellCounts.X % cellCounts.Y, n / (cellCounts.X * cellCounts.Y)));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: JitteredGridPattern3D): Array<Point3D>
        => JitteredGridPoints3D(self.Region, self.CellCounts, self.JitterAmount, self.Seed);

    // The k-th sample of stratum `s`, counted X fastest then Y then Z: uniform
    // within the stratum, its three coordinates from three independent streams.
    StratumPoint3D(region: Bounds3D, strataCounts: IntegerVector3, seed: Integer,
        s: Integer, k: Integer): Point3D
    {
        var i = (s % strataCounts.X).ToNumber + SampleUnit(seed, s, k * 3);
        var j = (s / strataCounts.X % strataCounts.Y).ToNumber + SampleUnit(seed, s, k * 3 + 1);
        var l = (s / (strataCounts.X * strataCounts.Y)).ToNumber + SampleUnit(seed, s, k * 3 + 2);
        return Point3D(
            region.Min.X + i * (region.Max.X - region.Min.X) / strataCounts.X.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Y + j * (region.Max.Y - region.Min.Y) / strataCounts.Y.ToNumber,
            region.Min.Z + l * (region.Max.Z - region.Min.Z) / strataCounts.Z.ToNumber);
    }

    // `samplesPerStratum` points in each stratum.
    // Precondition: every strata count is positive.
    StratifiedPoints3D(region: Bounds3D, strataCounts: IntegerVector3,
        samplesPerStratum: Integer, seed: Integer): Array<Point3D>
        => (strataCounts.X * strataCounts.Y * strataCounts.Z * samplesPerStratum).MapRange(n =>
            StratumPoint3D(region, strataCounts, seed, n / samplesPerStratum, n % samplesPerStratum));

    // The pattern's points.
    Points(self: StratifiedPattern3D): Array<Point3D>
        => StratifiedPoints3D(self.Region, self.StrataCounts, self.SamplesPerStratum, self.Seed);
```
